cohort: This study included 1552 consecutive women (mean age, 53 years) with a personal history of breast cancer and a negative prevalence surveillance breast MRI result between August 2014 and December 2016.
finding: BRCA mutation status, receipt of breast-conserving surgery, and adjuvant chemotherapy were significantly associated with the development of second breast cancers after negative surveillance MRI, while outcomes did not differ by surgery-MRI interval.
